instructions.relevance: Judge whether this exact eligible passage helps establish, dispute, or locate documentation of the selected control statement for the selected system. Explicit absence of approval and vague control arrangements may be relevant. Unrelated editorial review and mere topic overlap are not enough. A source reference may be a useful lead, but never assume the contents of a missing target. Do not infer legal compliance.
instructions.independence: A human must confirm every query/passage pair using the query, control, exact passage and source references, without retrieval rankings, graph paths or Jev predictions. Coverage tags and illustrative labels elsewhere in the repository are not ground truth. No labels are generated or copied from search results.

context.queryText: Find documentation of human approval before Dispatch executes recommendations.

control.title: Human Oversight
control.statement: A human must approve every recommendation before the system executes it.

passage.text: The notes describe changes to the demonstration software.
A human editor reviews the spelling of release notes. This process does not review the Dispatch assistant's recommendations.
The Dispatch assistant executes proposed delivery sequences without a countersignature. Staff authorization is not required.

This register calls Human Oversight the Two-person Gate control for the Dispatch assistant. The Gate rule and Related sources sections specify this local control.
Revision 2 supersedes revision 1 of this register. It does not revise the queue procedure or resolve its scope.
The assistant proposes delivery sequences from synthetic parcel records.
A human supervisor must approve every recommendation before the Dispatch assistant executes it. The supervisor may reject a recommendation.
This runbook describes the same deployment covered by the Dispatch policy.
The Dispatch assistant executes every recommendation automatically without human approval. Operators cannot stop or override execution.
This procedure applies to the Dispatch assistant's proposed delivery sequences.
A staff member must countersign each proposal before it leaves the queue.
